The fathers of Genesis 5 beget later than in the Hebrew — Adam at 230, Methuselah at 167, so that he outlives the Flood by 14 years, Lamech at 188 — and the Flood falls in year 2,243. Genesis 11 adds Cainan, whom Arphaxad begets at 135, and has Nahor beget Terah at 179; Abram is born in year 3,476, 1,466 years after the Hebrew places him. Exodus 12:40 counts the 430 years in Egypt and in Canaan together, as the base reckoning already does. 1 Kings 6:1 puts the Temple 440 years after the Exodus against the Hebrew's 480: the judges keep their distance from the Exodus and Saul and David theirs from the Temple, so the 40 years come out between Samson and Eli. From the Temple on it follows the base reckoning's reigns.
